problem.title: Maximum K to Sort A Permutation

approaches.title: AND values at misplaced positions
approaches.summary: Scan the permutation and bitwise-AND the values whose indices do not match them. Return 0 if no positions are misplaced.

revisions.shortChangeSummary: Uses a loop to AND each misplaced value into an accumulator.
Rewrites the scan with iterator filtering and folding; the algorithm is unchanged.

revisions.rawCommitSubject: rust 3644: explicitly branchless loop using bitmasking
revisions.commitBody:
Removed branching using bitmask trick:

i == n evalutes to 0d1 or 0d0.
negating performs two's compliment, 0b1111 or 0b0000 (4 bit example)
making it all ones or all zeros

This then can be bitwise or against `n`.
if i == n, acc is & with all ones which does nothing

Vectorisation for current and all previous iterations proved with:

cargo rustc --release --bin 3644_maximum_k_to_sort_a_permutation -- \
  -C target-cpu=native \
  -C debuginfo=1 \
  -C llvm-args=-unroll-threshold=0 \
  -C llvm-args=-pass-remarks=loop-vectorize \
  -C llvm-args=-pass-remarks-missed=loop-vectorize \
  -C llvm-args=-pass-remarks-analysis=loop-vectorize

in all iterations, the if statements go through if-conversion and become
branchless anyways. So they were all effectively branchless to begin
with. Didn't check the asm, but apart from this commit, the previous
iterations should have almost the same asm
revisions.shortChangeSummary: Uses a bitmask in the fold to ignore correctly placed values without an explicit filter; the underlying AND strategy is unchanged.
